fullPassage:
Save Coral Reefs

When you go deep into the sea, you can see a variety of marine animals including corals. Over the course of many years, corals build up to form large structures called coral reefs. Brightly colored coral reefs provide a beautiful underwater landscape. However, this is not the only reason they are valuable.

Importance of Coral Reefs

Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect both marine life and people living near the sea. Coral reefs provide shelter to an abundance of marine life, such as fish and underwater plants. Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs, they are often called "the rainforests of the sea." Nearly one quarter of all known marine species depend on coral reefs for survival — they hide themselves from predators, find food, reproduce, and raise their young in coral reefs.

As far as humans are concerned, over half a billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and survival. When large waves generated by storms rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they prevent the land on the shore from washing away and thus protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a source of medicine, and many organisms found in coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer. This is why they are sometimes referred to as the "medicine chests of the sea."

Coral Reefs in Danger

These underwater treasures are under threat of destruction. The more coral reefs become damaged, the more creatures relying on them will lose their homes. Thus, the increasing loss of coral reefs might lead to the destruction of the entire marine ecosystem. The U.N. reported that many of the world's coral reefs are currently endangered. In fact, nearly half of Australia's Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest, has disappeared. If swift action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050.

What causes coral reefs to die? There are various causes, like destructive fishing techniques, overpopulation of corals' natural enemies, and careless tourism. However, the leading cause is the rise in water temperature due to global warming. The ideal temperature range for corals to live is 20°C to 28°C. When the water temperature rises above 30°C, coral reefs turn white and eventually die. Another serious cause is plastic waste. Plastic products, such as bottles and fishing lines, have been dumped into the sea. This spreads viruses and diseases, damaging coral reefs and their inhabitants.

Technologies to Save Coral Reefs

In recent years, advanced technologies have been put in place to save coral reefs by monitoring, protecting, and restoring them in quick and efficient ways. Researchers from Florida introduced a soft jellyfish-like robot to monitor coral reefs without damaging their delicate bodies. In addition, an Australian research team invented an intelligent underwater robot to protect coral reefs from a dangerous species of starfish. The robot uses a camera and computerized vision system to scan the reefs and identify this starfish. When it encounters one, the robot uses a foldable arm to inject some toxic salt into the starfish and eliminate it. Meanwhile, 3D printing systems have been proposed in Hong Kong as one way to restore coral reef structures. The 3D printer creates artificial support for corals. An example is a block made of mud that lies on the floor of the ocean. It is shaped in a way that allows corals to attach to it and grow easily.

Actions to Save Coral Reefs

Here are some simple but effective steps we can take in order to help protect coral reefs. First, you can avoid using beauty products containing tiny pieces of plastic because they pollute the oceans. Also, try not to use sunscreen made with certain chemicals that damage corals. Second, you can volunteer to help clean the beach. Recycling and reducing trash is a huge help in maintaining a clean ocean. Last but not least, make it known that coral reefs are in danger by spreading the word to people around you. Let people know about the threat to coral reefs and what actions to take to save them. This will make a big difference for the future.

questions.passage: Brightly colored coral reefs provide a beautiful underwater landscape. However, this is not the only reason they are valuable. Coral reefs are crucial (A)[ecosystems / economies] that protect both marine life and people living near the sea. Coral reefs provide (B)[shelter / pressure] to an abundance of marine life, such as fish and underwater plants. Because of the (C)[diversity / division] of life found in coral reefs, they are often called "the rainforests of the sea." Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs, they are often called "the rainforests of the sea." Nearly one quarter of all known marine species depend on coral reefs for survival — they hide themselves from predators, find food, reproduce, and raise their young in coral reefs. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 산호초는 해양 생물과 바닷가 사람들을 보호하는 중요한 생태계이다. 산호초는 풍부한 해양 생물에게 보금자리를 제공한다. 생명의 다양성 때문에 '바다의 열대우림'이라 불린다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ecosystems — shelter — diversity
❌ ② economies — shelter — division
❌ ③ ecosystems — pressure — division
❌ ④ economies — pressure — diversity
✅ (A) ecosystems: 산호초는 '생태계'. economies(경제)는 맥락 불일치. ✅ (B) shelter: 해양 생물에게 '보금자리/피난처' 제공. pressure(압력)는 부적절. ✅ (C) diversity: 생명의 '다양성'. division(분할)은 맥락 반대.
det.tip: ecosystem(생태계) vs economy(경제). shelter(보금자리) vs pressure(압력). diversity(다양성) vs division(분할/분리).

questions.passage: These underwater treasures are under threat of (A)[destruction / construction]. The more coral reefs become damaged, the more creatures relying on them will lose their homes. Thus, the increasing loss of coral reefs might lead to the destruction of the entire marine ecosystem. The U.N. reported that many of the world's coral reefs are currently (B)[endangered / encouraged]. If (C)[swift / slight] action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이 수중 보물들은 파괴의 위협을 받고 있다. 유엔은 많은 산호초가 현재 멸종 위기에 있다고 보고했다. 신속한 조치가 취해지지 않으면 대부분 파괴될 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② destruction — endangered — swift
❌ ① construction — endangered — slight
❌ ③ destruction — encouraged — slight
❌ ④ construction — encouraged — swift
✅ (A) destruction: 'under threat of destruction' 파괴의 위협. construction(건설)은 반대 개념. ✅ (B) endangered: 멸종 위기에 처한. encouraged(격려받은)는 맥락과 어울리지 않음. ✅ (C) swift: '신속한 조치'. slight(약간의)는 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: destruction(파괴) ↔ construction(건설). endangered(멸종위기) ↔ encouraged(격려된). swift(신속한) ↔ slight(약간의).

questions.passage: This spreads viruses and diseases, damaging coral reefs and their inhabitants. In recent years, advanced technologies have been put in place to save coral reefs by monitoring, protecting, and (A)[restoring / restricting] them in quick and efficient ways. Researchers from Florida introduced a soft jellyfish-like robot to monitor coral reefs without damaging their (B)[delicate / deliberate] bodies. Meanwhile, 3D printing systems have been proposed in Hong Kong as one way to restore coral reef structures. The 3D printer creates (C)[artificial / artistic] support for corals. When it encounters one, the robot uses a foldable arm to inject some toxic salt into the starfish and eliminate it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 첨단 기술로 산호초를 모니터링, 보호, 복원한다. 해파리 로봇은 섬세한 몸을 손상시키지 않고 모니터링한다. 3D 프린터는 인공적인 지지대를 만든다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ restoring — delicate — artificial
❌ ② restricting — deliberate — artistic
❌ ① restoring — deliberate — artistic
❌ ④ restricting — delicate — artificial
✅ (A) restoring: 모니터링, 보호와 함께 '복원'. restricting(제한)은 맥락 불일치. ✅ (B) delicate: 산호초의 '섬세한' 몸. deliberate(의도적인)는 부적절. ✅ (C) artificial: '인공적인' 지지대. artistic(예술적인)은 맥락과 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: restoring(복원) vs restricting(제한). delicate(섬세한) vs deliberate(고의적인). artificial(인공적인) vs artistic(예술적인).

questions.passage: When large waves generated by storms rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural ①<u>barriers</u>. The force of the waves is ②<u>reduced</u> as they hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they ③<u>prevent</u> the land on the shore from washing away and thus protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a source of medicine, and many organisms found in coral reefs are used to ④<u>spread</u> diseases like cancer.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 산호초는 자연 장벽 역할을 하고, 파도의 힘을 줄이며, 해안을 보호한다. 산호초에서 발견되는 유기체는 암 같은 질병을 치료하는(treat) 데 사용된다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①barriers(장벽): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ②reduced(줄어들다): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ③prevent(방지하다): 원문 그대로, 적절. ❌ ④spread(퍼뜨리다): 원문은 treat(치료하다). 질병을 '퍼뜨리다'는 반대 의미.
det.tip: treat(치료하다) ↔ spread(퍼뜨리다). 'used to treat diseases'(질병 치료에 사용) vs 'used to spread diseases'(질병 확산에 사용).

questions.passage: What causes coral reefs to die? There are various causes, like ①<u>destructive</u> fishing techniques, overpopulation of corals' natural enemies, and ②<u>careless</u> tourism. However, the ③<u>leading</u> cause is the rise in water temperature due to global warming. When the water temperature rises above 30°C, coral reefs turn white and ④<u>gradually</u> die.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 파괴적인 어업, 무분별한 관광, 수온 상승 등이 원인이다. 수온이 30°C 이상이면 산호초가 하얗게 변하고 결국(eventually) 죽는다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④destructive(파괴적인): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ②careless(무분별한): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ③leading(주된): 원문 그대로, 적절. ❌ ①gradually(점차적으로): 원문은 eventually(결국). 맥락상 '결국 죽는다'가 자연스럽고 gradually는 '점차 서서히' 뉘앙스로 미묘하게 다르지만, 더 정확히는 eventually = '최종적으로'.
det.tip: eventually(결국, 최종적으로): 시간이 지나 최종 결과 강조. gradually(점차적으로): 변화 속도 강조. 원문은 '하얗게 변하고 결국 죽는다'로 최종 결과를 말함.

questions.passage: Researchers from Florida introduced a soft jellyfish-like robot to monitor coral reefs without damaging their delicate bodies. In addition, an Australian research team ①<u>invented</u> an intelligent underwater robot to protect coral reefs from a dangerous species of starfish. The robot uses a camera and computerized vision system to ②<u>scan</u> the reefs and ③<u>identify</u> this starfish. When it encounters one, the robot uses a foldable arm to inject some toxic salt into the starfish and ④<u>preserve</u> it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 호주 연구팀이 불가사리로부터 산호초를 보호하기 위해 지능형 수중 로봇을 발명했다. 로봇은 카메라로 산호초를 스캔하고 불가사리를 식별한다. 불가사리를 만나면 독성 소금을 주입하여 제거한다(eliminate).
det.analysis: ✅ ①invented(발명하다): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ②scan(스캔하다): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ③identify(식별하다): 원문 그대로, 적절. ❌ ④preserve(보존하다): 원문은 eliminate(제거하다). 해로운 불가사리를 '보존'하면 맥락 반대.
det.tip: eliminate(제거하다) ↔ preserve(보존하다). 해로운 불가사리를 제거하는 것이 목적이므로 preserve는 부적절.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.tip: abundance(풍부함) ↔ scarcity(부족, 희소). plenty, wealth, surplus 모두 '풍부함' 계열.

questions.stem: 'eliminate'의 영영풀이로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: to make something larger or more powerful
to keep something safe from harm or damage
to find or learn something for the first time
to completely remove or get rid of something

det.korean: 로봇은 독성 소금을 주입하여 불가사리를 제거한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④'to completely remove or get rid of': eliminate = 완전히 제거하다. ❌ ②'to make larger': 확대하다 = enlarge. ❌ ③'to keep safe': 보호하다 = protect. ❌ ①'to find for the first time': 발견하다 = discover.
det.tip: eliminate = remove = get rid of: 제거하다, 없애다.

questions.stem: 'Consequently'의 영영풀이로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: as a result of what has just been stated
in a way that is not expected or planned
in spite of what has been mentioned before
at the same time as something else happens

det.korean: 파도의 힘이 줄어든다. 결과적으로, 해안이 쓸려나가는 것을 방지한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①'as a result of what has just been stated': consequently = 결과적으로. ❌ ②'not expected': 예상치 못하게 = unexpectedly. ❌ ③'in spite of': ~에도 불구하고 = nevertheless. ❌ ④'at the same time': 동시에 = meanwhile.
det.tip: Consequently = As a result = Therefore: 결과적으로, 따라서.

questions.passage:
This is why they are sometimes referred to as the "medicine chests of the sea."

Coral Reefs in Danger

These underwater treasures are under threat of destruction. The more coral reefs become damaged, the more creatures (__________) on them will lose their homes. Thus, the increasing loss of coral reefs might lead to the destruction of the entire marine ecosystem.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오.

The more coral reefs become damaged, the more creatures (rely) on them will lose their homes. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 산호초가 손상될수록, 산호초에 의존하는 더 많은 생물이 보금자리를 잃을 것이다.
det.analysis: creatures를 수식하는 현재분사 relying. rely → relying (현재분사, 능동). 'creatures relying on them' = 그것들에 의존하는 생물들.
det.tip: 현재분사(V-ing)는 명사를 뒤에서 수식할 때 '~하는'의 의미. rely → relying.

questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오.

Meanwhile, 3D printing systems have been (propose) in Hong Kong as one way to restore coral reef structures. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 한편, 3D 프린팅 시스템이 산호초 구조물을 복원하는 한 가지 방법으로 홍콩에서 제안되었다.
det.analysis: 수동태 'have been + p.p.' 구조. propose → proposed (과거분사, 수동). 주어인 3D printing systems가 제안을 '받는' 것이므로 수동태.
det.tip: have been + p.p. (현재완료 수동태). propose → proposed. '제안되다' = be proposed.

questions.passage:
Save Coral Reefs

When you go deep into the sea, you can see a variety of marine animals including corals. Over the course of many years, corals build up to form large structures called coral reefs. Brightly colored coral reefs provide a beautiful underwater landscape. However, this is not the only reason they are valuable.

Importance of Coral Reefs

Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect both marine life and people living near the sea. Coral reefs provide shelter to an abundance of marine life, such as fish and underwater plants. Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs, they are often called "the rainforests of the sea." Nearly one quarter of all known marine species depend on coral reefs for survival — they hide themselves from predators, find food, reproduce, and raise their young in coral reefs.

As far as humans are concerned, over half a billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and survival. When large waves generated by storms rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they prevent the land on the shore from washing away and thus protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a source of medicine, and many organisms found in coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer. This is why they are sometimes ____ as the "medicine chests of the sea."

Coral Reefs in Danger

These underwater treasures are under threat of destruction. The more coral reefs become damaged, the more creatures relying on them will lose their homes. Thus, the increasing loss of coral reefs might lead to the destruction of the entire marine ecosystem. The U.N. reported that many of the world's coral reefs are currently endangered. In fact, nearly half of Australia's Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest, has disappeared. If swift action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050.

What causes coral reefs to die? There are various causes, like destructive fishing techniques, overpopulation of corals' natural enemies, and careless tourism. However, the leading cause is the rise in water temperature due to global warming. The ideal temperature range for corals to live is 20°C to 28°C. When the water temperature rises above 30°C, coral reefs turn white and eventually die. Another serious cause is plastic waste. Plastic products, such as bottles and fishing lines, have been dumped into the sea. This spreads viruses and diseases, damaging coral reefs and their inhabitants.

Technologies to Save Coral Reefs

In recent years, advanced technologies have been put in place to save coral reefs by monitoring, protecting, and restoring them in quick and efficient ways. Researchers from Florida introduced a soft jellyfish-like robot to monitor coral reefs without damaging their delicate bodies. In addition, an Australian research team invented an intelligent underwater robot to protect coral reefs from a dangerous species of starfish. The robot uses a camera and computerized vision system to scan the reefs and identify this starfish. When it encounters one, the robot uses a foldable arm to inject some toxic salt into the starfish and eliminate it. Meanwhile, 3D printing systems have been proposed in Hong Kong as one way to restore coral reef structures. The 3D printer creates artificial support for corals. An example is a block made of mud that lies on the floor of the ocean. It is shaped in a way that allows corals to attach to it and grow easily.

Actions to Save Coral Reefs

Here are some simple but effective steps we can take in order to help protect coral reefs. First, you can avoid using beauty products containing tiny pieces of plastic because they pollute the oceans. Also, try not to use sunscreen made with certain chemicals that damage corals. Second, you can volunteer to help clean the beach. Recycling and reducing trash is a huge help in maintaining a clean ocean. Last but not least, make it known that coral reefs are in danger by spreading the word to people around you. Let people know about the threat to coral reefs and what actions to take to save them. This will make a big difference for the future.
questions.stem: 다음 우리말에 해당하는 영어 단어를 (2단어) (영어로) 쓰시오. 산호초에서 발견되는 많은 유기체는 암 같은 질병을 치료하는 데 사용된다. 이것이 산호초가 때때로 "바다의 약상자"라고 불리는 이유이다. → '불리다, 언급되다'에 해당하는 영어 표현 2단어: __________ __________ as

det.korean: 산호초가 때때로 바다의 약상자라고 불리는(referred to) 이유.
det.analysis: 'be referred to as ~' = '~라고 불리다/언급되다'. refer to A as B = A를 B라고 부르다. 수동태에서 referred to as.
det.tip: refer to A as B → A is referred to as B. '~라고 불리다'의 핵심 표현.
